pr_title: Perf(hpy): drop the per-launch dependency probe
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 3 of 3 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: test_launch_never_probes_schema_libraries is behavioral: a logging shim records every interpreter call hpy makes, and the exact two-call count (start probe plus exec) fails on any reintroduced import probe, not just one naming the three libraries.
The hpy test also proves exit-code pass-through through the logging shim (SystemExit(5)), so the shim cannot silently swallow the exec.

test_missing_pydantic_is_one_line_and_exit_2 hides pydantic via sys.modules[...] = None in a real subprocess, with no stubbing of the code under test, and asserts exit 2, no traceback and a single stderr line naming pydantic; argparse errors (CaptureError, exit 1) or a late import traceback would both fail it.
Both tests reuse the existing plugin_root fixture and the _run/_posix helpers and shim pattern already proven on Windows in test_interpreter_path_with_spaces_launches.
The probe sits after the sys.path insert and before the first harness_lib import, so a missing pydantic is caught at the earliest point with no traceback; the line stays within the 110-column limit.
A subprocess test stubs sys.modules['pydantic'] = None to exercise the real failure path rather than mocking the helper.
README hpy paragraph matches the new hpy behavior: the launcher no longer probes dependencies, and the interpreter order and python3-stub skip are unchanged.
The hook claim is accurate: validate_pr_json_schema.py:278-281 writes a one-line warning and exits 0 when jsonschema or referencing is absent.
The hpy header comment, README and test_launch_never_probes_schema_libraries all state the same contract; plugin.json is bumped to 0.4.1.
test_launch_never_probes_schema_libraries is behavioral and can fail: a logging shim records every interpreter call hpy makes, so re-adding any dependency import probe, or an extra launch, breaks it.
The schema hook claim in README.md matches the code: validate_pr_json_schema._missing_validator stands down with one stderr line naming the missing module (hooks/validate_pr_json_schema.py:254-281).
test_pr_review_missing_pydantic simulates the missing module with sys.modules['pydantic'] = None and runs the real script through runpy, with no stubbed helpers.
hpy's header comment, the README paragraph and the 0.4.1 patch version bump move together, and the post-forcepush pre-flight still gives an explicit opt-in dependency check.

important.name: Missing-pydantic exit breaks the driver's documented failure contract
important.summary:
The module docstring (line 76-78) and main() (lines 1959-1971) promise that every failure, an argument error included, exits 1 with one `problem: ...` line per defect on stderr. The new probe at lines 124-128 prints a bare `pr_review: pydantic>=2 ...` line (no `problem:` prefix) and calls sys.exit(2). Skills and agents that read pr_review output for `problem:` lines or treat exit 1 as the failure signal will not recognise it, and tests/scripts/test_pr_review_missing_pydantic.py pins the exit 2 / no-prefix behavior, so the contradiction is locked in.

Also (overall): The new import probe prints `pr_review: pydantic>=2 is required ...` and exits 2. The module docstring (pr_review.py:77-78), main()'s docstring (pr_review.py:1960-1961) and pr-review SKILL.md:48 all promise that every failure exits 1 with `problem: ...` lines on stderr, and an exit 1 is the STOP signal. _Parser (pr_review.py:1909-1917) exists specifically to turn argparse's exit 2 into exit 1. A caller following the skill sees an exit code and a stderr format the procedure never mentions. The new test (tests/scripts/test_pr_review_missing_pydantic.py:19) locks the exit 2 in place.

Also (overall): Before this PR, hpy warned on every launch when jsonschema/referencing were missing. The PR drops that warning, and the hpy header (hpy:9-10) and README.md:94-97 now say the code that needs these modules reports their absence itself. pr_review.py only probes pydantic, though. Its review writer imports jsonschema and referencing lazily inside review_merge._cached_validator (review_merge.py:477-478). With them missing, capture, merge and amend all succeed, and then build, a fold after build, or closeout dies with an uncaught ModuleNotFoundError traceback. main() only catches CaptureError/ValueError/FileNotFoundError (pr_review.py:1966-1969), so no `problem:` line is printed. That contradicts the README claim and leaves a half-finished run.

Also (runtime): The message says `pydantic>=2 is required`, but `import pydantic` succeeds on a v1 install. review_models.py:21-29 then fails on `from pydantic import ConfigDict, field_validator, model_validator` with a raw ImportError traceback, which is the failure this probe exists to prevent. The probe also reports `pip install pydantic`, which would not upgrade an installed v1.
fix: Emit `problem: pydantic>=2 is required for the review models (pip install pydantic)` and exit 1 (update the assertions in tests/scripts/test_pr_review_missing_pydantic.py to match)
Keep exit 2 but add it to the module docstring as the one documented exception, with the message format

Change the probe to `print("problem: pydantic>=2 is not installed; the review models need it (pip install pydantic)", file=sys.stderr)` followed by `sys.exit(1)`, and update the test to assert returncode 1 and `lines[0].startswith("problem:")`.
Keep exit 2 but document it as the single exception in the pr_review.py module docstring, main()'s docstring and pr-review SKILL.md:48.

Extend the probe at pr_review.py:124-128 to loop over ("pydantic", "jsonschema", "referencing") and name the first missing module in a single `problem:` line before any subcommand runs, and add a test case that sets sys.modules['jsonschema'] = None.
Alternatively, narrow README.md:94-97 and the hpy header to say only pydantic is checked up front and jsonschema/referencing fail at the first review write.
Probe `from pydantic import ConfigDict` (or check pydantic.VERSION major >= 2) in the same try/except, and word the message `pip install 'pydantic>=2'`

minor.name: README overstates missing-module reporting for jsonschema/referencing
minor.summary: README.md:57-59 says the code that needs jsonschema / referencing / pydantic reports a missing module itself, and that pr-review / pr-team exit with a message naming it. Only pydantic is covered: pr_review.py:124-128 probes pydantic alone. jsonschema and referencing are imported lazily in review_merge._cached_validator (review_merge.py:477-478), which pr_review.py reaches when it validates review JSON, with no ImportError handling. With the hpy warning removed, a pr_review.py run without jsonschema fails with a raw ModuleNotFoundError traceback at that point. The parenthetical limits the claim to pydantic, but the sentence reads as covering all three packages.
fix: Narrow the README sentence to say pr-review / pr-team exit with a message naming a missing pydantic, and that a missing jsonschema / referencing surfaces as an ImportError from the validating step.
Extend the availability probe in plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py (lines 124-128) to cover jsonschema and referencing, with a test alongside tests/scripts/test_pr_review_missing_pydantic.py.

minor.name: Driver leaves sys.argv as ['-c', script, '--help'], so pr_review.py never sees the '--help' the test passes
minor.summary: DRIVER runs the script with runpy.run_path but does not shift sys.argv, so inside pr_review.py sys.argv[1:] is [<script path>, '--help'], not ['--help']. Today the pydantic probe at plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py:124-128 exits before argument parsing, so the outcome is unaffected, but the '--help' argument is decorative and the launch does not mirror a real `python pr_review.py --help` invocation. If the probe ever moved behind parse_args, the script path would be parsed as an invalid subcommand and the test would fail for an unrelated reason (CaptureError exit 1) instead of exercising the help path.
fix: Shift argv in the driver so the script sees its own argv: "import runpy, sys; sys.modules['pydantic'] = None; sys.argv = sys.argv[1:]; runpy.run_path(sys.argv[0], run_name='__main__')".
